rv.q: These knowing flourishes distinguish Deadly Stages as an ingenious cavalcade of nostalgia where the possibility of Vera Charles snatching a role from Veronica Traymore incites a burst of audience laughter.
The thing that makes Deadly Stages work, and what ultimately won me over, is that it avoids what it knows it cannot achieve–the perfection of a well-written farce.
Although Deadly Stages has amusing moments, it is a tired retread of better and more subtle works in this genre.
The predictable resolution of the mystery sends one out of the theater wondering why this play was necessary—and whether All About Eve is streaming tonight.
Deadly Stages is all that its title promises.

cn.t: Critics split sharply on this campy backstage murder mystery spoof, with some finding it uproarious and packed with clever references, while others dismiss it as cheesy and comedically challenged.
